intro: Multi-agent isn't magic — it's a way to slice the problem so each piece fits in one model's context and capability. The slice shape (the topology) controls cost, latency, observability, and failure modes. Most 'multi-agent' systems are actually one of six shapes.

items.title: Supervisor
items.whenToUse: Heterogeneous tasks where a routing decision drives downstream specialization. The pattern this /ask page uses.
items.mechanism: Lightweight supervisor classifies the request and hands off to one of N specialists. Each specialist has its own tools + system prompt.
items.tradeoff: One extra hop of latency. Concentrates intelligence cost on the work, not the routing. Easy to debug because handoffs are explicit.

items.title: Swarm
items.whenToUse: Long-running collaborative tasks where any agent can pick up where another left off.
items.mechanism: Shared task queue, any agent may pop. Each can hand off to a named peer mid-task. State lives in the queue, not in any one agent.
items.tradeoff: Resilient, parallel. Hard to reason about who's doing what; observability is non-trivial.

items.title: Pipeline
items.whenToUse: Tasks with a fixed processing order: extract → transform → critique → publish.
items.mechanism: Output of agent N is input to agent N+1. Often the simplest 'multi-agent' system is really a multi-stage pipeline.
items.tradeoff: Trivial to debug, predictable cost. Adds no resilience over a single-agent chain — it's just chaining.

items.title: Hierarchical
items.whenToUse: Big tasks decomposed into sub-tasks, each of which may itself need decomposition.
items.mechanism: Manager agent dispatches to sub-managers, who dispatch to workers. Results bubble up.
items.tradeoff: Scales to large tasks. Recursion depth must be bounded or cost explodes. Inter-level handoff is the hard part.

items.title: Debate
items.whenToUse: Tasks where a robust answer benefits from adversarial review (legal analysis, security review, code review).
items.mechanism: Two or more agents argue different sides. A judge agent picks a winner or synthesizes.
items.tradeoff: Surfaces edge cases a single agent misses. Slow and expensive. Diverge the agents on prompt or model — same model + same prompt = no debate.

items.title: Blackboard
items.whenToUse: Open-ended problems with many possible contributors and unclear ordering.
items.mechanism: Shared blackboard (write-only structured store). Each agent watches for triggers, writes its contribution. Optional controller schedules.
items.tradeoff: Maximally flexible. Maximally hard to operate. Reserve for problems where you genuinely can't define the topology up front.

items.title: Subagent delegation (context isolation)
items.whenToUse: When the parent agent's context window is the bottleneck — long horizon, dirty intermediate state, exploratory sub-tasks.
items.mechanism: Parent spawns a child agent with a fresh context to do a bounded sub-task. Child returns a compressed result. Parent never sees the intermediate state. Exactly the Claude Code `Task` pattern.
items.tradeoff: Different motivation from the other topologies above — here the goal is context HYGIENE, not specialization. Pay one round-trip to keep the parent's context clean.

pitfalls.title: Multi-agent when one would do
pitfalls.body: Three agents that could be one prompt chain. Multi-agent multiplies cost + complexity; reach for it when one model's window or capability becomes the bottleneck.

pitfalls.title: Shared-state races
pitfalls.body: Swarm and blackboard topologies invite write races. Either serialize through a queue or design idempotent writes.

pitfalls.title: Inscrutable handoffs
pitfalls.body: If you can't trace 'this answer came from agent A → B → C with these arguments at each hop', you cannot debug it. Build SSE-style trace from day one.

pitfalls.title: Infinite handoff loops
pitfalls.body: Agent A hands to B, B hands back to A, A hands to B again. Track handoff chain depth; abort beyond a small cap (3–5).

pitfalls.title: Debate without divergence
pitfalls.body: Two instances of the same model debate and quickly converge. Use different models, different roles, or different system prompts.
